scores.evidence: Figure 1 (compaction flowchart, TD) has Japanese labels that are easy to read at both widths (pages/desktop-jp-06.png, pages/mobile-jp-09.png). The term, comparison and failure-pattern tables fit in 2 columns at 390 px with nothing cut off (pages/mobile-jp-06.png, pages/mobile-jp-10.png, pages/mobile-jp-12.png, pages/mobile-jp-13.png). Every screen has a heading, figure, table, code block or check (textOnlyScreens empty), and there are no hard failures in metrics.json.

The page has a steady rhythm: concept, then term table, then comparison table or figure, then an inline check (1/5 to 5/5). There are no walls of text, and the step lists put each expected result in a short separate box (pages/mobile-jp-15.png, pages/mobile-jp-16.png, pages/desktop-jp-10.png). Desktop JP median is 39 chars per line, inside the 30–40 target.

All visible text is in Japanese, with English shown only as glossary glosses (session, context window, compaction). Contrast is good, and the 1–4 keyboard hints and option numbers are visible. No controls sit under the top or bottom bars (pages/mobile-jp-30.png, pages/mobile-jp-34.png). No overflowX, console or mermaid errors, unknown blocks or broken images.

niceToHave: On mobile, the 'auto compaction' row of the 5-2 comparison table breaks as '起きたら、指示が / 残っているかを確かめる', which leaves a short ragged line. A slightly shorter cell text, such as '自動で起きる。指示が残ったか確かめる', would wrap more evenly (pages/mobile-jp-06.png).

In practice step 3, the inline chip '/compact 作ったファイルとその役割を中心に残して' is longer than the 390 px line, so it wraps inside its own box. It stays readable, but a shorter focus such as '/compact ファイルと役割を残して' would keep it on one line (pages/mobile-jp-25.png).

reader: the mobile full-length PNG stops at 16000 px, and the per-screen PNGs were used instead. 13 failed /api/ requests (500 on progress, events and notifications) are environment noise and are not counted as console errors.
